count_note: docs/dev/e59/WINDOWS.md lists 4 windows for this lane's 26 files: action-dynamic.mjs askDynamicDifficulty (328), action-murder.mjs performDirectMurder (321), dice-look.mjs diagnoseDiceLook (537), rules.mjs openRulesManager (490). This file has 21 surfaces: 13 module windows (those 4, plus chooseVariant's three in this lane - the crisis menu, Search, Infiltrate - promptForNote, and the actionWindow calls of the betrayal, Listen's room, Force, Pick and Tail), 1 Daggerheart window the module locks (the roll window), 6 chat-card surfaces (the GMs' away card, the unwitnessed line, Daggerheart's chat menu, the Dynamic GMs' card, the ruling buttons action-pipeline.mjs builds, the Reroll's re-asked card) and the shared frame. The difference is the tool's reading, not missing windows: its OPENERS regex (scripts/tests-windows.mjs:45) matches `drpgWindow(` and not `(columns ? actionWindow : drpgWindow)(` (action-menus.mjs:230, 522) or an `actionWindow(` call, so every action window is counted once, as ui-columns.mjs wideWindow (WINDOWS.md:221) and, where they wrap it, not at all. WINDOWS.md's line numbers also differ from today's source for three of the four (askDynamicDifficulty 327, performDirectMurder 323, diagnoseDiceLook 538; the file is dated 14.11, dice-look.mjs changed 16.11); `node tools/e59/windows.mjs --check` was not run and is not called by tools/check.mjs or a workflow (grep). Not in this file though named by the lane: Rest's window (action-rest.mjs, its rows from action-facilities.mjs), Dynamic's first window (call-gm.mjs promptForRequest), Observe, Analyze, Frisk and Tamper (controls-04). The unwitnessed line is counted as a control (a status line), the only one that is not pressed. No base-run.json, probe-42.json or probe-43.json existed when this file was written: no test result is cited as read.

findings.title: The roll window does not redraw when the roller's last Sanity is marked while it stands open: no disadvantage on the window, the GM's draw throws it and flags the honest roll
findings.surface: Daggerheart's roll window, as the module locks it
findings.what_happens: The window's disadvantage comes from advantageSources (:1091), which adds Breakdown (stateGrant, isBrokenDown: remaining Sanity <= 0) on each render. The only redraw the module asks for is on updateActor whose change carries flags.drpg (:131); a Sanity mark is a change of system.resources, and the Breakdown state that follows is a status effect toggled by the primary (states.mjs:400 toggleStatusEffect), not a flag. So the window keeps showing no disadvantage. The primary GM's draw reads Breakdown when it throws (roll-draw.mjs:2295, the `breakdown` reader) and throws the disadvantage die; the claim the window configured has none, so checkRoll pushes an `advantage` flag (:2423-2425), whispered to the GMs (tellUnexpected:2456) and named to the roller.
findings.failure_scenario: A player opens a Search's roll window at 1 Sanity left; the GM marks that last Sanity for a scene beat before the player presses Roll; the window still shows a normal roll, the dice come back at disadvantage and the GMs get a whisper that the roll's advantage differed from what the GM counted.
findings.expected: the window redraws on a change of the roller's Sanity (or of any value advantageSources reads), so the window shows what the GM throws
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another redraw: Daggerheart's window is an ApplicationV2 not bound to the actor (the harness's glue is the only copy here; Daggerheart's source not read), and nothing else in roll-dialog.mjs calls app.render. Looked for a module flag on Breakdown: states.mjs reconciles with toggleStatusEffect, an effect, not flags.drpg. stateGrant is not pinned to the first render the way windowCalls is, so a redraw would show it: the gap is the listen alone. A Breakdown that lands between the press and the draw is the same flag and is not this window's fault; the window's open time is what widens it. Not measured: the harness has no real roll window.
findings.probe: Open a student's action roll window at Sanity 1 (a player client), mark the last Sanity from the GM's sheet, read .disadvantage-chip.selected (expected true, read false), press Roll and read game.drpg.rollFlags() on the GM

findings.title: 'Rolls with no GM connected': on a second GM's chat log Grant all and Grant none stay after the first GM decided, and a press there does nothing and says nothing
findings.surface: Rolls with no GM connected - the GMs' card
findings.what_happens: The card is whispered to every GM. A press takes the buttons off the pressing GM's copy at once (:3050) and asks the primary to decide; decideNow updates each listed roll message (granted, author) but never the card, so no other GM's copy is rerendered and its buttons stay. A press there removes them, asks the primary, and awayRowOf returns null for every row now decided: askToDecide answers [], which no caller reads, and nothing is said.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs are connected when a player's rolls from the empty table are listed; GM A presses Grant all; GM B, reading the same card a minute later, presses Grant none, sees the buttons vanish and believes the Hope was withheld, while it was already granted.
findings.expected: the card redrawn on every GM once its rolls are decided (no buttons, and which way it went), or a press on a decided card that says so
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether a roll message's update rerenders the card: Foundry rerenders only the updated message, and the card is another message. Checked the second press: decideNow skips rows whose stamp holds `granted` (awayRowOf:2838), so no double grant - the defect is the stale buttons and the silence. Scenario 15-held A3 presses on one GM only (15-held.mjs:646-656).
findings.probe: Two GM clients with a stamped roll: press Grant all on gm0; read gm2's rendered card for .drpg-away-actions (expected gone, read present); press Grant none there and look for any notice

findings.title: A roll thrown with no GM keeps saying 'a GM decides later' after a GM granted it or did not
findings.surface: A roll thrown with no GM connected - its own roll card's line
findings.what_happens: The line is drawn whenever the message carries the stamp; a decision writes `granted` into the same flag (decideNow:2968), which rerenders the card on every client, and the test reads the flag's presence, not its `granted`. So the roller and the GMs read 'it moves no Hope, Sanity, or Despair for now. A GM decides later ...' on a roll whose Hope was granted.
findings.failure_scenario: A player rolls a statistic with no GM connected, the GM returns and presses Grant all, the player's Hope goes up, and their roll card still says it moves nothing and waits for a GM.
findings.expected: the line follows `granted`: granted, not granted, or waiting
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another line or key for a decided roll: DRPG.Rolls has unwitnessed and the away* keys only (en.json read for the five keys used here); no ROLL_STATES row for a granted stamp is used in onRenderUnwitnessed. No test reads the card after a decision (grep of tests-tier*.mjs and scenarios for roll-state="unwitnessed").

findings.title: The rules manager never redraws: its Save puts another GM's rewording back, and its Withdraw withdraws a motive it does not show
findings.surface: Killing game rules - the GM's manager
findings.what_happens: The window draws rules() and motive() once. Save sends every drawn row's field text, changed or not, and saveRulesEdit maps today's list onto it, so a rule another GM reworded meanwhile gets the words drawn at open back; a rule added meanwhile (another GM, or a New Rule Despair Call carried out by addRule) is kept but never shown. Withdraw calls setMotive(null) on whatever is in force.
findings.failure_scenario: GM A has the manager open while GM B rewords rule 2 and saves; GM A ticks Revoke on rule 4 and saves; rule 2 is back to its old words and 'Saved - 3 rules in force' is all either GM is told.
findings.expected: the window redraws on killingGameRules and the motive's setting (keeping typed words), or Save writes only the rows the GM changed
findings.refutation_tried: alreadyOpen (:465) keeps one copy per browser, not per table. No updateSetting hook or keepLive in rules.mjs (grep). The second GM's case needs two GMs; the New Rule Call's case (a rule not shown) needs one GM and a Monokuma player. R1520 tests Withdraw with a stand-in, not a change under an open window.
findings.probe: Two GMs: open the manager on gm0; on gm2 updateRule(id, 'B'); on gm0 press Save; read rules() (expected 'B', read the old text)

findings.title: Dice look's Copy report closes the window and says nothing, a failed copy included
findings.what_happens: The button's callback starts the copy without awaiting it (void), answers 'copy', and DialogV2 closes the window. The other two Copy report buttons await the copy, say 'Copied' and bring their window back (diagnostics.mjs openReport:2324-2331; gm-panel.mjs:770-777).
findings.evidence:
secondary: [{ action: "copy", label: game.i18n.localize("DRPG.Diagnose.copy"),
    callback: () => { void game.clipboard?.copyPlainText?.(text); return "copy"; } }],
findings.failure_scenario: A player asked by the GM to send their dice look presses Copy report, the window vanishes with no word, and on a browser that refuses the clipboard nothing was copied and nothing says so.
findings.expected: as the Diagnose window: awaited, said, and the window kept
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether Foundry's copyPlainText says anything itself: not read in Foundry's source (not in this checkout); both other callers add their own notice, which suggests it does not.
findings.probe: game.drpg.diagnoseDiceLook(); press [data-action=copy]; look for a notice and whether the window stays

findings.title: A Reroll of an action a GM rules on posts a second card and leaves the first card's buttons live (suspected)
findings.surface: Reroll of an action a GM rules on - the re-asked card
findings.what_happens: For Observe, Analyze, Direct Murder and a described Search the Reroll posts a new card with Reply alone and the line that the previous answer no longer stands; the first card is not settled. Where it was not yet answered, its buttons (Nothing was there, Refuse the attempt, an Observe's picks, Create an item) stay on it, about the roll that was replaced, while the new card offers only Reply. A Dynamic success's card is ended by the Reroll (withdrawDynamicFind); these are not.
findings.failure_scenario: A player rerolls a described Search before the GM answered; the GM sees two cards, presses Refuse the attempt on the first, and the action is handed back for a roll the player has already replaced and paid three Hope to redo.
findings.expected: the first card ended or greyed as a Dynamic's is, its mechanical answers moved to the re-asked card, or the GM told on the first card that it no longer stands
findings.refutation_tried: Read settleGmRuling whole: no settleCall, no lookup of the first card. Not traced: which buttons each first card carries (Observe's and Analyze's cards are built in other lanes' files) and what each reads at the press after a Reroll; a ruling already given is said to stand by the code's own comment (:1955-1957).
findings.probe: Search 'something specific' on p1, Reroll before the GM answers, read both cards' [data-drpg-call] buttons on gm0, press decline on the first and read the actor's actions

findings.title: Comments name an action window that is gone: 'Move's briefing' is still listed as an actionWindow caller
findings.surface: An action's window - the shared frame
findings.where: scripts/action-menus.mjs:278 and :304-305; .claude/rules/code.md's action-briefing.mjs row ('Move's own briefing window (`briefing`)')
findings.what_happens: The Move window was removed by E100 item 1 (action-briefing.mjs:327-329, action-rolls.mjs:77-83); performAction(actor, 'move') returns null (:303). The frame's header and its half-width branch still name it as the window that asks nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer looking for the window the half-width branch serves finds none: no caller in scripts/ passes an empty `ask` today (the actionWindow calls in action-murder, action-listen, action-doors and action-tail all pass one).
findings.expected: the comments say the branch has no caller, or the branch goes
findings.refutation_tried: grep of scripts/ for actionWindow( callers: action-menus.mjs (chooseVariant, promptForNote: both pass ask), action-murder.mjs:253, action-listen.mjs:174, action-doors.mjs:67, 123, action-tail.mjs:48 - each with ask. Callers outside this lane (action-project.mjs, action-rest.mjs, palm.mjs ...) not read for an empty ask.

not_established: No control was pressed in this pass (no harness run). Each row is label -> element -> listener -> handler -> effect as read in source; tests and scenarios are named from their text, their results not read (no base-run.json).

What a GM's press of Daggerheart's own 'Reroll Action Roll' on a player's drawn roll leaves standing: reroll-receipts.mjs judgeRewrite keeps a GM's rewrite as the roll's dice (:109-112) and private-rolls.mjs onRollsRewritten relays them; roll-draw.mjs has no updateChatMessage hook, so the GMs' record (store rolls) and the action's result look to stay on the first dice. New live check: a GM rerolls a player's Search roll from the chat menu; read the card, game.drpg.rollFlags(), the store rolls' record and the item granted.

Finding 10's road: which buttons the first ruling card of Observe, Analyze and a described Search carries after a Reroll, and what each applies when pressed then (cards built in action-observe.mjs, action-analyze.mjs, action-search.mjs, read by other lanes).

The betrayal's confirmation reads the Eclipse before it opens (action-murder.mjs:240) and uses that reading after Yes (:271-288): an Eclipse that begins or ends while it stands open sends the betrayal the other way (now, or parked). Whether requestBetrayal's run on the GM refuses the mismatch was not read (bridge-runs-acts.mjs betrayal run).

Finding 1 at a table: whether Daggerheart 2.12's roll window redraws itself on its actor's update (its source is not in this checkout); if it does, the module's forceConfig would draw the Breakdown and the finding falls. LIVE-E16-01 covers the wrapper, not this.
Finding 9: whether Foundry v14's game.clipboard.copyPlainText notifies by itself (not in this checkout).

Themes: the scan reads rules by selector text; a rule that hides a control through a broader selector (a whole .application or chat-message rule) is not caught by it. No window was drawn (LIVE-E59-01 is the drawn one).
